_note: Campfire smoke (docs/design/fire_smoke_wind_design.md; Dave 10 Nov 2026: 'its hovering around like flies. it should be drifting away with the breeze'). Each puff leaves the flames rising at rise_m_s for the fire's tier (small, medium, large) and moving with the world wind (weather_look.gd set_fire_air: speed and where it blows toward). It rises more slowly as it goes, down to rise_end_share of its start by the end of its life_s, and spreads (it grows grow_to times its start size, puff_m by tier) and fades. In near calm (wind under calm_mps[0], bending from there to calm_mps[1]) it goes straight up at calm_rise_m_s at least. On a still clear night it rises at night_rise_m_s and stops at about night_top_m, spreading flat. spread_deg is the cone the puffs leave in, [calm, windy]. No noise steers the puffs (the old turbulence turned each puff's velocity toward a random noise direction within a second, so the puffs wandered round the fire like flies).
_note_plume: Steve 10 Nov 2026, after Dino's small-fire shot (plume_small_shore_calm.png: no smoke to see above a small fire by day): alpha 0.2 -> 0.35, puff_m +0.15 each, amount 90/130/190 -> 120/150/200, so the column shows dark and dense at the flames. Dave 10 Nov 2026 ('make fire smoke actually look and act more like fire smoke'): one continuous plume, not puffs. amount is many small overlapping puffs (each only alpha of the full density), starting puff_m wide and growing grow_to times (narrow at the fire, wide up high). Each puff is near_grey at the fire and far_grey by the end (dark and dense low, light and thin high); fade is the density over its life [[life share, density]...]. wind_start_share: a fresh puff rises on its heat with only this share of the wind, and the wind takes it fully by the end of its life, so the plume bends over more the higher it goes. waver_m: the column sways this far by the end of its life, the same at the same height (one wavering column, not jitter). coals: the thin wisp from a bed of glowing coals.
_note_column: Steve 10 Nov 2026, after Dino's reshoot on 261a75eb (night: a column of separate round orange puffs; small fire by day: a haze drifting over the trees, faint at the fire). The puffs scattered apart (spread_deg 8 to 14 degrees) faster than they grew (the old size curve was flat at the start), so they never joined. Now: spread_deg 3 to 6; grow_shape puts 55% of a puff's growth in its first fifth of life (straight lines, [life share, growth share]); puff_m 0.6/0.7/0.8; each puff soft to its rim (shader); full density by 0.4 s (fade); far_grey 0.62 and an earlier fade-out, so the thin end is less of a pale mist and the plume reads from the fire up. Light: the sun and moon light the smoke fully; a fire's or lamp's light is greyed by light_grey and cut to fire_light, so the column is grey lit from below, not orange. alpha stays 0.35: it does reach the material; the 0.2 Dino measured was the old squared puff edge times fade 0.65 at a third of the life.
_note_small: Steve 10 Nov 2026, after Dino's reshoot on 9f728854 (plume_small_day: the one-rock-ring fire laid a haze as wide as the lake). The small tier only, by its own row in each per-tier list: puffs 0.3 m (a hand or two wide at the flame, 0.15 m at the start), growing 4 times not 8, half the density, living 0.6 of life_s (12 s), and 90 puffs: a thin wisp that climbs two or three metres before it thins out (0.4 and 60 were near-invisible by day on 75f0e27e). density and life_share are per tier (1, 1 for medium and large; the coals keep their own density and a full life). Rise and wind are unchanged (Jamie's Briggs heights); medium and large are as #958.
_note_tall: TEST-011, Dave's playtest 12 Nov 2026 ('Campfire smoke looks good near the fire but disappears around tree-canopy height. Smoke should rise above surrounding trees, gradually spread, and dissipate naturally... visible from a reasonable distance, including from nearby hills'). The near plume above lives life_s (20 s) and slows as it rises, so it thinned out by about 7 to 11 m in a calm and 5 m in a breeze, under the crowns (15 to 35 m). tall: a second, sparse plume on every lit campfire. Its puffs leave the flames with the near plume but are unseen for their first 6% of life (fade), then carry the column on: rise_m_s by tier in a breeze (at least calm_rise_m_s in a calm), slowing to rise_end_share by the end of life_s (70 s; heights and wind: _note_tall_height, _note_tall_wind), growing grow_to times from half of puff_m (about 8 m wide by the end) and fading. On a still clear night it stops at night_top_m and spreads flat. Lighter than the near plume (near_grey to far_grey), alpha per puff. Limits: amount puffs per fire (tens), stepped at fixed_fps (interpolated; the warm start is life_s x fixed_fps steps), and only the max_fires lit fires nearest the camera draw it. view_wide_m and view_high_m: the box the engine culls it by. Fires within 100 m (server_items.gd NEAR_M) come whole; those 100 m to 2 km off come as far_fires (protocol 114) and get this column alone, the far_max_fires nearest within the terrain view distance.
_note_tall_height: Dave 13 Nov 2026: 'smoke should rise at least twice the height of the average tree before it starts to dissipate to much.' The average tree in flora.json (mean of each species' height range, weighted by its per_hectare over all biomes) is about 19 m (21 m in the temperate forest), so twice is about 38 to 42 m. The tall plume now rises faster (rise_m_s 1.2/1.5/1.8 in a breeze, calm_rise_m_s 1.6), lives 70 s and keeps three quarters of its thickness to 55% of its life (fade): a medium fire's smoke is still that thick at 42 m in a calm (about 30 s) and in a 2 m/s breeze (about 32 s), and fades above. On a still clear night it stops at night_top_m 45. amount is raised with life_s (the same puffs a second); fixed_fps 8 keeps the warm start at 560 steps.
_note_tall_wind: Dave 13 Nov 2026: 'smoke plums have to be strongly effected by the wind as well. strong wind the smoke stays low and sideways. low wind it climbs higher and dissipates slower.' Up to wind_low_mps (a light breeze) the tall plume rises at rise_m_s and keeps its full fade (the twice-the-average-tree rule holds there). Above it the rise is cut to 1 / (1 + the wind over wind_low_mps / wind_rise_mps), never under min_rise_m_s (a medium fire: 1.5 m/s at 2 m/s wind, 0.5 at 5, 0.3 at 8), and everything after its thickest point is squeezed into 1 / (1 + the wind over wind_low_mps / wind_fade_mps) of the rest of its life (0.5 at 6 m/s, 0.4 at 8): in a strong wind it lies low, streams downwind and tears apart sooner. far_max_fires: how many far fires (far_fires, past 100 m) draw their smoke at once.
